lead.hed: U.S., Japanese, and Australian troops closed Orient Shield 26 in Hokkaido
lead.insight: DVIDS, posted Thursday: soldiers from Alaska's 11th Airborne Division, Japan's Northern Army, and Australia's 1st Division held the closing ceremony at Camp Higashi-Chitose on Sept. 24. The week included a first joint airborne drop of about 260 U.S. soldiers from five C-130Js, and a Sept. 22 live fire of HIMARS and Japan's multiple-launch rocket system at Yausubetsu. Closing ceremony, not a deployment order.
lead.image_credit: Master Sgt. Raymond Boyington · DVIDS 9962235 · Public domain · Australian, Japanese, and U.S. troops after the Orient Shield 26 closing ceremony, Hokkaido, Japan, Sept. 24, 2026.

political.hed: The Navy opened a Virginia center to train sailors on unmanned systems
political.insight: Defense News, Friday: Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Daryl Caudle cut the ribbon Thursday at the Robotic and Autonomous Systems Warfighting Development Center on Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story. He said a prototype is not combat power until a trained sailor can employ a reliable system. New training center, not a ship count.

political.hed: A new indictment names Mexican state officials in a cartel case
political.insight: Heritage, Friday: the commentary says the administration shifted from targeting cartel workers to a Justice Department indictment that names ten past and present officials of Mexico's ruling party in Sinaloa, including Governor Rubén Rocha Moya. All ten have denied wrongdoing. Commentary on an indictment, not a new statute. Not a ship story.

political.hed: Chinese warships blocked a Philippine resupply run at Second Thomas Shoal
political.insight: USNI News, Friday: Chinese warships and coast-guard cutters tried to hinder a Philippine resupply mission to Second Thomas Shoal on Thursday. Manila's National Task Force called it the most significant development at the disputed feature. Report of a blocked run, not a treaty change.

tech.hed: A Friday essay treats the data-center fight as a loss of confidence in providence
tech.insight: American Reformer, Friday: Chris Johnson writes that town-hall fights over data centers are about more than the machines. He cites protests in Louisville and Mercer County, Kentucky, and argues the panic tracks a people who no longer trust God's providence. Essay, not a zoning vote.

tech.hed: A Friday essay says progressive narratives spent the summer getting caught out
tech.insight: Law & Liberty, Friday: the piece says mainstream progressive stories took public blows at the end of summer, from congressional hearings on Anthony Fauci to the WNBA's unfinished answer on who may play. Essay, not a court ruling.

culture.hed: A review of Sam Brownback's book on China's war on faith
culture.insight: WORLD, posted Thursday: the review covers China's War on Faith, co-authored by former ambassador-at-large Sam Brownback. It says bishops are held under house arrest, pastors are imprisoned, and people in the pews are sent to reeducation camps. Review, not a new State Department designation.

culture.hed: A Friday essay traces the friendship behind U.S. religious-freedom law
culture.insight: Public Discourse, Friday: Thomas Farr writes that Frank Wolf and Chris Smith met in Bucharest in 1985 and later wrote the 1998 International Religious Freedom Act and the 2016 Frank Wolf revision. The Religious Freedom Institute will give them this year's Defender of Religious Freedom award. Essay, not a new statute.
